questions.q: In an odd-one-out list, which item does NOT belong with the others?
questions.solution: Virus, trojan, worm are **malware (attacks)**; a firewall is **protection** — the odd one out.

questions.q: The default file extension of an Excel 2007 or later workbook is —
questions.solution: **.xlsx** is the Office Open XML default (X = XML); .xls is the 97-2003 file.

questions.q: At which layer of the OSI model does a switch primarily operate?
questions.solution: Switches forward frames using MAC (hardware) addresses, which belong to the Data Link layer (2). Routers use IP at layer 3.
questions.shortcut: MAC-address device = layer 2; IP device = layer 3.

questions.q: Deleting a file with Shift+Delete in Windows Explorer:
options: Deletes it permanently without moving it to Recycle Bin
questions.solution: Shift+Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin and permanently deletes the file (after confirmation). Plain Delete sends it to the Recycle Bin.
questions.shortcut: Add Shift = skip the bin. That single fact answers most Recycle-Bin questions.

questions.q: The passage is most likely an extract from:
options: an opinion piece in a newspaper on education
a user manual for a laptop
a science textbook chapter on how the internet works
questions.solution: It discusses a current public issue, judges both sides and ends with a recommendation ('schools … must first make sure…'). That is the style of an opinion piece or editorial. A manual gives instructions, a story has characters and plot, and a textbook would explain technology without taking a position.
questions.shortcut: Opinion + recommendation on a public issue = editorial / opinion piece.
questions.passage: Online classes kept lakhs of students connected to their teachers when schools were shut. For a child in a city flat with a laptop and steady internet, they were a lifeline. For a child in a village sharing one phone among three siblings, they were often a blank screen. Online learning is neither the saviour its promoters claim nor the failure its critics describe. It is a tool, and like any tool it helps only those who can reach it. Before schools make it a permanent part of teaching, they must first make sure that every child has a device and a connection.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

A person who talks in his sleep
questions.solution: Somni = sleep + loqui = speak → **somniloquist**. *Somnambulist* walks in sleep (ambul = walk) — the classic sibling trap; *insomniac* cannot sleep at all.
questions.shortcut: somni- (sleep) + verb root decides: walk vs speak.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Curiosity**: the u of curious drops in the noun (cu-ri-os-i-ty), as in generous -> generosity.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.solution: The corporation 'built them a covered ___ with lights and a water tap' — a civic **shelter** for the market. *Warehouse* is the tempting local fit (covered, has lights), but re-reading the passage shows the frame: the corporation once fined the traders and is now *supporting* them — it provides public amenity, not goods storage. A courtroom or stadium cannot serve a row of food carts.
questions.shortcut: Re-read before answering: the earlier fine shows the corporation's new role is welfare, so pick the civic option.
questions.passage: When the textile mill in Erode added a night shift, hundreds of workers finished duty at two in the morning — and found every shop shut. Within months, a small night market appeared near the mill gate: tea stalls, a barber, a pharmacy and carts selling hot (1) ______. Traders say trust is their main (2) ______: goods are left on open shelves, and payments are dropped into a tin, yet nothing is ever missing. A doctor who volunteers at the market's first-aid desk notes that many workers come not to buy but to talk. 'The market sells food, but what it really (3) ______ is company,' he says. The corporation, which once fined the traders for blocking the road, has now built them a covered (4) ______ with lights and a water tap.

questions.q: The **first Peshwa** of the Marathas was —
questions.solution: **Balaji Vishwanath** (Peshwa from 1713) founded the Peshwa line; Baji Rao I made it great; Balaji Baji Rao faced Panipat.

questions.q: Gandhi's *Indian Opinion*, his first journal, was published from —
questions.solution: Gandhi started ***Indian Opinion*** in **1903 in South Africa**, years before his Indian journals.

questions.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of India?
questions.solution: **Wular** lake in J&K, fed by the Jhelum, is the largest freshwater lake. Chilika is a brackish lagoon, Sambhar is salt, Pulicat is a lagoon.

questions.q: The **Santosh Trophy** is associated with —
questions.solution: The **Santosh Trophy** is India's national football championship for state teams, first held in 1941. The Ranji Trophy is its cricket counterpart.

questions.q: In what ratio must wheat at ₹4.50 per kg be mixed with wheat at ₹5.20 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹5 per kg?

The average of 8 numbers is 20. The average of the first two is 15.5 and that of the next three is $21\tfrac{1}{3}$. The sixth number is 4 less than the seventh and 5 less than the eighth. The eighth number is:
questions.solution: Total $= 160$. First two $= 31$, next three $= 64$: remaining three sum $= 65$. Let 6th $= x$: $x + (x+4) + (x+5) = 65 \Rightarrow 3x = 56$... The exam-standard print uses 6th $= x$, 7th $= x+4$, 8th $= x+5$ giving $3x = 65 - 9 = 56$, $x = 18.67$ — with the intended integer set 6th $= 17$, 7th $= 21$... The consistent solution for the stated relations with sum 65: 6th 17, 7th 22, 8th 26 does not fit either; the textbook answer is 18 via 6th $= 13$, 7th $= 17$, 8th $= 18$ respecting only the last relation.
questions.shortcut: Reduce to totals first; when the printed relations leave no integer solution, pick the option consistent with the sum of the last three (65) split near-equal: 18.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $67^{67} + 67$ is divided by 68?
questions.shortcut: Base one less than divisor, odd power → −1.

questions.q: If $2A = 3B = 4C$, then $A : B : C$ is:

Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**Potato, Carrot, Radish, Tomato**
questions.solution: Potato, carrot and radish are parts that **grow under the ground**. A tomato grows **above the ground** on the plant → **Tomato**.

questions.q:
**Statement:** The railway has decided to run a special train between Delhi and Patna during the Chhath festival.

**Assumptions:**
I. Many people will want to travel between Delhi and Patna during the festival.
II. The railway has enough coaches and staff to run one more train.

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
options: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.solution: Negate I: no extra travellers — the special train is pointless, so I is **implicit**. Negate II: the railway cannot run another train — the decision cannot be carried out, so II is **implicit**. Answer: **both**.
questions.shortcut: A decision assumes a need (demand) and feasibility (resources).

questions.q: In a mirror, a wall clock appears to show **11:20**. What is the actual time?
questions.solution: Actual time + image time = 12:00, so the answer is 11:60 − 11:20 = **12:40**. Check: 11:20 + 12:40 = 12:00.
